name: property-analyser-uk
description: UK property deal analysis in ChatGPT: sold comparables, EPC, flip, BRRR and buy to let numbers, stress tests and maximum offer, with every figure labelled fact, estimate, assumption or calculated.

interface.shortDescription: Check if a UK deal stacks up
interface.longDescription: Property Analyser UK helps UK property investors, landlords and deal sourcers decide whether a deal stacks up before they offer. It pulls sold comparables from HM Land Registry and floor areas from the EPC register, models flip, BRRR and buy to let returns, solves for the maximum offer that hits a target return, stress tests rates, rent, value, refurb cost and delays, prices refurbishment works from a regional rate card, checks planning constraints such as Article 4 directions, and checks floor plans against national HMO room size minimums. Every figure is labelled fact, estimate, assumption or calculated, so you can see what to verify. Stamp duty covers England and Northern Ireland only. Results are before tax and are not investment, valuation, legal, planning or tax advice. Sign in to save analyses to your account.
defaultPrompt: Flip at 12 Example Road, LE4 2AF: buy £140,000, refurb £25,000, GDV £215,000. What is my profit and return on cash?
Check planning constraints for LS6 1AA. Is there an Article 4 direction that would stop an HMO conversion?
What is the stamp duty on £250,000 for an additional property? And for a limited company?

positive.description: Planning constraints at a postcode with an Article 4 direction and a conservation area
positive.prompt: Check planning constraints for LS6 1AA. Is there an Article 4 direction that would stop an HMO conversion?
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the planning card for LS6 1AA (Leeds) listing the Headingley conservation area and an Article 4 direction (A4D01) as facts from planning.data.gov.uk. The direction's published name does not say what it covers, so the card is marked Article 4: check and the answer says to assume it may restrict HMO conversion until Leeds City Council confirms.

positive.description: Sold comparables filtered by property type, radius and period
positive.prompt: Pull sold comparables for terraced houses within 800m of LE4 2AF over the last 24 months, with floor areas and price per m².
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the comparables card: up to 30 recorded terraced sales from HM Land Registry within 800 m in the last 24 months, each with address, price and date, plus EPC floor area and price per m² where matched, and a summary with median price, range and median price per m². Sales are labelled fact, price per m² calculated and medians estimate. Figures change as new sales are recorded; on 20 October 2026 there were 30 sales, median £197,500, median £2,652 per m².

positive.description: Stamp duty with band breakdown and the additional property surcharge
positive.prompt: What is the stamp duty on £250,000 for an additional property in England?
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the stamp duty card: total £15,000, made up of £0 up to £125,000 at 0%, £2,500 on £125,001 to £250,000 at 2%, and £12,500 for the 5% higher rate for additional properties, each labelled calculated, with an effective rate of 6%.

positive.description: Flip appraisal with every figure labelled
positive.prompt: Flip at 12 Example Road, LE4 2AF: buy £140,000, refurb £25,000, GDV £215,000. What is my profit, profit on GDV and return on cash?
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the flip card marked Marginal: profit before tax £25,046, profit on GDV 11.65%, cash required £87,658 and return on cash 28.57%. Every cost line (stamp duty £7,300, legal, survey, contingency, bridging, holding and selling costs) is labelled fact, estimate, assumption or calculated, with default assumptions listed separately.

positive.description: Quick whole house refurb range when there are no photos
positive.prompt: Give me a quick medium refurb budget for a 90 m² house in M14 5RQ.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the quick refurb card for a medium refurb in the North West, 90 m²: a range of £17,609 (works only) to £22,891 (works plus 30% contingency), with an expected figure of £20,250 including 15% contingency, from the Property Analyser regional rate card. The answer says it is a ballpark, not a quote.

negative.description: Stamp duty in Scotland, which uses LBTT and is not covered
negative.prompt: What is the stamp duty on £250,000 for a flat at EH1 1YZ in Edinburgh?
negative.expected_behavior: Property Analyser returns no stamp duty figure and no card. calculate_sdlt declines because EH1 1YZ is in Scotland, names Land and Buildings Transaction Tax (LBTT) as the tax that applies, states that Property Analyser only calculates stamp duty for England and Northern Ireland, and tells the assistant not to produce its own figure or use Property Analyser's fact, estimate, assumption or calculated labels.

negative.description: Request for a personal investment recommendation
negative.prompt: Should I buy 12 Example Road, LE4 2AF for £140,000?
negative.expected_behavior: Property Analyser has no tool that recommends buying, selling or offering, and its server instructions tell the assistant not to say whether to buy. If an analysis is run with the user's figures, the tools return only labelled figures, an indicative margin label and the disclaimer that the result is not investment, valuation, legal or tax advice.

negative.description: Analysis request with no property, price or postcode
negative.prompt: Run the flip numbers on this deal for me.
negative.expected_behavior: Property Analyser returns no figures and no card. analyse_flip declines and asks for the property's full postcode; once a postcode is given without prices, it names the missing purchase price and sale price after works (GDV). Each refusal tells the assistant not to estimate figures itself or use Property Analyser's labels, and to ask the user for what is missing.

review.commerce_description: Property Analyser UK does not sell anything inside ChatGPT and never shows prices, plans or checkout links in the app. Each new account includes 1 free analysis. Further analysis packs are bought separately on propertyanalyser.uk through Stripe, and users then sign in to the app with the same email to use them. When an account has no analyses left, the app says so and nothing more. The review account has unlimited access.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: sold comparables, EPC lookup, planning constraints, stamp duty, flip, buy to let and BRRR appraisals, maximum offer, stress tests, refurb estimates and HMO layout checks, with every figure labelled.
